steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F ( 190 degrees C). Grease baking sheets.

Beat butter and sugar together in a medium bowl until lighter in color. Gradually beat in egg substitute and vanilla. Sift gluten- free flour mix, baking soda, baking powder, and salt together; stir into butter mixture until blended. Finally, stir in the chocolate chips.

Drop spoonfuls of cookie dough 2 inches apart on prepared baking sheets. Bake in preheated oven until edges are golden brown, about 6 to 8 minutes. Let cookies cool on baking sheet for a few minutes before removing to wire racks.

raw_recipe.headline: Gluten-Free Chocolate Chip Cookies
raw_recipe.description: These easy gluten-free chocolate chip cookies bake up golden and chewy for a delicious sweet treat with gooey chocolate chips in every bite!

review.reviewBody: My kids and I loved them! You cannot tell the difference. We used 1/2 cup cornstarch, 1/2 cup brown rice flour and 1 1/4 cup white rice flour for the baking mixture. I used a real egg. I also added 1 tablespoon milk because they were thick and cooked 10 min. They were fabulous!

I am newly GF and knew I couldn't do this without a good chocolate chip cookie. This is the first one I tried and won't waste my time on any others. It was PERFECT! Dare I say as good as AP Flour cookies? They were soft and rose very well! 
*If you had trouble with them rising make sure your soda is NEW, less than 2 months old. It should flow out of the box (don't scoop) with no clumps. I never use butter, always margarine (tub or stick, I used a tub this time) and have never had a problem. It is already soft and chilled. Put your baking sheet in the freezer each time before you drop the cookies so they don't spread before entering the oven. I also chill my dough between batches. 
Here is how I made mine:
Tub butter
Same type/amount of sugars
Regular vanilla extract (not a celiac so i'm not too worried)
2 eggs
Same baking soda
NO baking powder
1/2 tsp salt
1/2 C quick oats
1/2 bag of chopped nuts and chocolate chips

GF Baking Mix:
1 1/2 cups white or brown rice flour
1/2 cup potato starch (not potato flour)
1/4 cup tapioca flour
1 tsp xanthan gum

Made 1 1/2 times the recipe.
Followed advice re: adding an extra 1/2 cup of flour (before “doubling”) & using some potato starch in place of some of the flour & decreasing the brown sugar by 1/4 cup.
Used 1 regular egg + 1/8 cup sweet potato purée (since i made 1 1/2 batches...needed another “1/2 egg” or 1/8 cup of a substitute).
I also used 2/3 butter & 1/3 margarine to reduce spreading.
Used Pamela’s gluten-free All-Putpose Flour.
Baked for 10 minutes, flipping the trays at 5 minutes.
These are fabulous!
They held their shape really well. I prefer a more toothsome cookie - i think that subbing ground oatmeal & adding chopped pecans or walnuts would accomplish this.
Otherwise...making notes because I will definitely wanna make these AGAIN!

Even though I made a goof and added too much extra flour mixture, I'm giving a 5 star rating. I also reduced the white sugar to 1/2 cup. I salvaged my dry cookie dough by pressing them flat with a glass dipped in water ( a little trick I learned from my mother a long-time Baker). I baked the flattened cookies at 350 for 10 minutes. the result was a soft baked cookie that goes well with a cup of coffee or a glass of coconut milk.
next time I will be adding extra flour a little at a time as I should have known to do to begin with. 
these cookies have great flavor and great versatility for those who have a gluten-free, dairy free diet. 
This made a big batch of cookies that I shared with the office. Even after confessing my mistake everyone agreed they were still a yummy cookie. and were especially surprised when I told them they were gluten and dairy free.

I used 1 egg and 1/2 C corn starch, 1/2 C brown rice flour, 1 1/4 C white rice flour, and 3/4 tsp. xantham gum for the baking mix. Dropped by 1/2 Tablespoonfuls onto baking sheet, but they hadn't spread 6 min. in, so I flattened with a fork. Flavor was WONDERFUL, but they were dry and a bit crumbly, so I'll adjust it more in the future - probably an extra egg (most recipes this size have 2 anyway) and a dash of milk, or use the 40% whole grain flour : 60% white flours/starches I've read about (so 1 C brown rice flour, 1 1/4 C some ratio of white rice flour and corn starch). Two children and I who can all tolerate gluten fine, along with the one who can't, all thought they tasted great!

I have tried TONS of different CC cookie recipies and these are definitely far and away the best. I did modify it by using Earth Balance. I also used Bob's Red Mill all purpose GF baking flour. My egg replacer is 2 tbsp ground flax seed soaked in 3 tbsp of water. It is also possible to find vegan Chocolate Chips, but I indulged and used chips from Ghiardelli. Cooking times were on the longer end, but I watched closely. I think the reason these are so good is there is a lot more chips, butter, sugar, and salt in these than typical recipes.

I loved them! I used a real egg instead of egg replacement, and I used brown rice flour and tapioca flour for the baking mix. I baked them for about 15 minutes before they were completely done in the middle. They were a little crumbly, but they were crispy and delicious!

I made these cookies today exactly as listed in the recipe except :I used Bob’s Red Mill 1 to 1 gluten free flour (has xanthan gum in it already).I used one large egg plus an egg white instead of egg replacement.*Press the dough on the cookie sheet rather than leaving a mound of dough. If you press them, they spread perfectly !Nice and crisp around the edges and chewy inside. I added a photo! I’ll make these again for sure!
I used 1 1/2 C Ancient Grains gluten free flour, 1/2 C tapioca flour, 1/4 cassava flour. Didn't add the white sugar. And added 1C Craisins and 3/4 C chopped walnuts. Also used 2 eggs. DELICIOUS!

i made these for choir and everyone loved them. i used 2 real eggs instead. and king Arthur gluten free flour and they turn out perfect. also cook them for 9 or ten minutes if you do it for the time that is says the are really under done

I'm Gluten, egg and dairy free. I used Smart Balance for butter, Gluten-free Bisquick for the baking mix and dairy free choc chips. I also found the dough to be crumbly so I added 1/4 to 1/2 C applesauce and that helped a lot...and I can't taste it either. The dough tastes great! And the cookies are a bit crunchy on the edges but wow, they're great!! :) Thanks!!
The best Gluten-free recipe ever ! I used a little less sugar and plant based chocolate chips. (SOY free) .
easy and good cookies
These were very good and easy to make. The GF family member prefers Alton Brown's "The Chewy Gluten Free", which is excellent - tastes better than a regular cookie!

Great recipe! I’m making it for a gluten-free friend and they turned out amazing! They are crispy around the edges and chewy in the middle, the hard part is waiting for them to cool and not eating them all myself. I did substitute two eggs for the egg substitute like many recommended, they spread out pretty thin, but we like them that way. I also used Bob’s Red Mill gluten-free baking/all purpose flour. I think this will be a keeper for gluten-free things.
I used two eggs my chickens work to hard for me to substitute that also used coconut sugar not white sugar used less brown sugar to keep them fluffy
Only thing I changed was egg substitute for real eggs, and I put two - came out great, even in my old oven!

These cookies are delicious and I can't really tell that they are gluten-free. Baked beautifully! I used 2 eggs instead of the egg substitute as one user suggested. I also used some butterscotch chips. Thanks!
These were moist, spread like a regular cookie and my husband loved them. I usually bake cookies on the light side, but these cookies needed the full bake time.
Delicious alternative to cookies made with white flour. I added pecans too.
